claims.text: Overall tribo-corrosion degradation in high-entropy alloys is governed by dynamic disruption and regeneration of a protective passive film.
The passive film is composed of multiple alloying-element-derived components.
Mechanical wear continuously breaches the passive film.
Fresh alloy substrate exposed by film breach corrodes more rapidly than the film-covered surface.
The alloy's electrochemical response regenerates the passive film after disruption.
Coupling between film removal and film regeneration produces more degradation than the sum of isolated wear and corrosion.
The initial high-entropy alloy has a uniformly distributed passive film.
The initial passive film is self-healing.
Under the proposed tribo-corrosion conditions, mechanical wear removes the passive film faster than it can reform.
Accelerated corrosion causes localized surface weakness or embrittlement.
Corrosion-induced surface weakness or embrittlement exacerbates mechanical wear.
The reciprocal acceleration of corrosion and wear establishes a positive feedback loop that increases total degradation.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion will produce statistically greater total degradation than the sum of static-corrosion damage and inert-medium wear damage.
The prediction applies when a protective passive film forms and is mechanically disruptable.
The predicted synergy may fail when the passive film is too mechanically robust to be removed.
The predicted synergy may fail in mildly corrosive media, when corrosion kinetics are too slow, or under very low wear stresses.
The magnitude of synergistic degradation depends on alloy composition, film-formation kinetics, and mechanical load.

contradictions.description: The design says all three test sets should maintain identical mechanical loading parameters, but one control explicitly receives no mechanical wear, so mechanical loading cannot be identical across all sets as written.
